name: Mike Elizondo
sources: HipHopDX — The players of Dr. Dre's 2001 — https://hiphopdx.com/editorials/the-players-of-dr-dres-2001-where-are-they-now/
Gearspace — Death Row / g-funk bass players — https://gearspace.com/board/rap-hip-hop-engineering-and-production/1287837-did-dr-dre-90s-death-row-g-funk-producers-play-his-own-bass-hire-bassist.html
notes: The *post*-g-funk low end, and the research is explicit that this is not the 1992–96 era — he was documented as still a student then, so this entry is windowed 1999–2004 and is deliberately the contrast partner to the Colin Wolfe / Tony Green session entry rather than a duplicate of it. The whole model is one comparison made numeric: simpler, tighter, root-motion-focused, less syncopated than the 1992 playing, and locked to a quantized kick. So where that entry has `independent_riff` at `followRootsProb` 0.3 and `glideProb` 0.7, this one has `mirror_kick` at 0.9 with glide at 0.1 — the audible difference between 1999 and 1993 West Coast bass, per the research, is exactly that lock. His lines are chord-tone-strict with chromatic approach notes rather than blues-pentatonic, which is why `passingTones` carries `m2` — the only entry in this batch that does — and why `scales` drop minor pentatonic and blues for natural and harmonic minor. He realizes a keyboard writer's harmony and doubles the piano's bass motion, so the melody is `warm_grand_piano` in a low register with a very high `chordToneBias`, and the countermelody is `octave_echo` for the documented unison bass/keys hooks. His part is continuous, so `dropOutBeats.prob` is cut. ⚠ `medium` is the research's own rating and it names the gap: role and era documented, workflow detail limited, so the drum-side numbers here are inherited rather than authored. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 46 to 45 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 46 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 1.
